title: Oscar®-Qualifying HollyShorts Film Festival 2026
deck: The festival, painted by hand, then built across Hollywood.
location: TCL Chinese Theatres and Ovation Hollywood
lede: For its 22nd edition, HollyShorts got a poster painted by hand: the festival itself, from the red carpet to the screen. Its dancing figures then walked onto every badge, sign and bottle.
challenge: The 22nd Annual Oscar-qualifying HollyShorts Film Festival ran from Aug. 13 to 23, 2026, at the TCL Chinese Theatres in Hollywood. Eleven days and two sites, the theaters and Ovation Hollywood, meant a long list of surfaces, from a tower billboard to a wine label, all needing one look.
work: The poster came first, as a hand painting of the festival: the red carpet, the audience, the screen, the Chinese Theatre and the Ovation Hollywood arch. Two details from the painting became the system. The dancing figures on the painted screen moved onto the badges, merchandise and signage, and the 22 was drawn as a film strip, in white and black.

The figures do the wayfinding, from the Red Carpet sign on Hollywood Boulevard to the tower signs in the Ovation Hollywood walkway and the theater's directional signs. At full scale the art wrapped the Hollywood and Highland tower, hung over the Ovation Hollywood entrance and ran on building and directory screens.

Eight badges, one for each pass type, share the system. So does the festival trophy, a film-strip frame that holds the winning film's poster. The edition had its own wines, a Sauvignon Blanc, a Chardonnay and a Cabernet Sauvignon, with labels taken from the poster and bottled by Artiste Winery. Online, the social campaign ran to hundreds of graphics under the same direction.

credits: Dalton Corr: art direction, poster painting, logo, badges, merchandise, wine labels, production design, on-screen creative, social creative direction
press: The Contending: the official 2026 poster reveal, with a design credit.
The festival was covered by Deadline, WWD, HELLO!, The Hollywood Times and others.
